description: Buyid confederation of emirates (934–1062) founded by Daylamite warlords from the Caspian coast who captured Baghdad (945) and reduced the Abbasid caliph to a figurehead; as Shia rulers governing a Sunni caliph, the Buyids pioneered the Shia-Sunni administrative compromise that characterised many later Islamic dynasties, while their patronage of Arabic and Persian literature supported scholars including Avicenna and al-Biruni.

temporal.notes: Stub: dates from GeoJSON basemap years 1000–1200

lifecycle_phases.description: Buyid (Buwayhid) brothers conquered Persia from Daylamite highland base, seizing Baghdad in 945 and placing the Abbasid caliph under nominal rule.
Greatest territorial extent under Adud al-Dawla; major patronage of Persian literature, philosophy, and Shia scholarship.
Rival Buyid princes divided the empire; Seljuk pressure from the east steadily reduced territories.
Final Buyid ruler expelled from Baghdad by Seljuk Tughril Beg; dynasty ended.

rise_factors.description: Daylamite infantry were elite mountain fighters able to defeat Arab cavalry armies.
Buyids were Shia and used patronage of Shia shrines to build religious legitimacy in Iraq and Persia.
Abbasid caliphate's military collapse allowed Buyids to become kingmakers in Baghdad.

decline_factors.description: Buyid princes divided territories among sons, creating competing courts that fought each other.
Seljuk Turks overwhelmed Daylamite infantry with superior cavalry and numbers.
